name: Abel
overview: Abel, the son of Adam and Eve, is remembered in Scripture primarily for his righteous faith and the sacrifice he offered to God, which was deemed more excellent than Cain's and testified to his righteousness (Hebrews 11:4). His tragic death at the hands of his brother Cain marks the first shedding of innocent blood, a significant event referenced by Jesus as a symbol of righteous suffering (Matthew 23:35, Luke 11:51). Additionally, the name Abel is associated with a notable location, the 'great stone of Abel,' where the ark of the LORD was placed, underscoring the historical and spiritual significance connected to this name (1 Samuel 6:18).
